how_stored_and_keyed.table: One DynamoDB table (default name irpt-requests, ycharts/generate/acceptance.py:50-53; the table name is an ARGUMENT of the script) with partition key `tenant` (the owner's firm code) and sort key `request_revision`. Every row below is a request_revision prefix.
how_stored_and_keyed.UPLOAD#<upload_id>: infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/intake/uploads.py:262-270 (row built), :296 (published): upload_id = 'UP-'+hash(firm, principal, token) (:260); members filename, content_sha256 (sha256 of the original bytes, :261), artifact_ref (the retained original), and for a template upload file_type and source_lane='TEMPLATE_UPLOAD' (:268-270). A CSV upload carries NO source_lane member: that absence is its lane marker (read_input derives CSV_UPLOAD from it, :526).
how_stored_and_keyed.original_bytes: infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/intake/uploads.py:287-291: artifacts.put(family ORIGINAL_HOLDINGS for a template, ORIGINAL_CSV for csv). reports/repository.py:397-441: the put writes the object to S3 and publishes an ARTIFACT#<artifact_id> row (artifact_id = 'ART-'+digest of owner, family, logical id: :419 and _binding) holding ref{artifact_id,family,sha256,version_id,byte_length,...} and blob{bucket,key,version_id}. reports/repository.py:551-558: the bytes are read by GetObject(Bucket,Key,VersionId) from the blob member. The digest is the sha256 of the bytes, in ref.sha256 and in the UPLOAD# row's content_sha256.
how_stored_and_keyed.NORMALIZATION#<upload_id>#<hash(options): infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/intake/uploads.py:305-307 and :349 (input_id member added on acceptance); deferred form :377 and :423-469 (state RESOLVING / NEEDS_CORRECTION / NORMALIZED). The script does not read these rows.
how_stored_and_keyed.INPUT#<input_id>: infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/intake/uploads.py:352-366 (_publish_frozen; row at :359-362): input_id 'portfolio_'+sha256, members identity, owner, upload_id, artifact_ref (the NORMALIZED_PORTFOLIO artifact, :354-356) and content_sha256. Only uploads.py publishes INPUT# rows (one writer in the product tree).
how_stored_and_keyed.template_stored_at_acceptance: infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/intake/portfolio.py:498-499: the normalized document (schema irpt-normalized-portfolio.v2) holds `template` = the reader's output at acceptance; the document is the bytes of the NORMALIZED_PORTFOLIO artifact (uploads.py:354-356). read_input compares read_template(original) to document['template'] at uploads.py:538.
how_stored_and_keyed.lane: INPUT# rows exist for two lanes only, TEMPLATE_UPLOAD and CSV_UPLOAD (the only INPUT# writer is uploads.py:359; custody inputs are frozen from a custody snapshot, intake/custody_portfolio.py:229-239, and no INPUT# row is written for them in the product tree). The script reads the lane from the UPLOAD# row (source_lane). Custody and mail inputs are NOT in the table scan and are not counted.
how_stored_and_keyed.RETENTION#: rows of the retention index (reports/retention.py); the script does not read them.

how_a_report_is_tied_to_an_input: Through the accepted request's composition, not the request row. ycharts/generate/acceptance.py:62 keys an accepted request as request_revision 'analysis#REQ-<24 hex>#1'; its record (acceptance.py:115-120, a JSON string in member `record`) holds accepted_at (epoch seconds), composition_ref (the REQUEST_COMPOSITION artifact: ycharts/generate/submission_service.py:137-139) and browser_sha256 (a digest only, so the record alone does not name the input). The composition document (ycharts/generate/submission.py:191-193, retained as artifact bytes) holds browser.input_id (public field, submission.py:16) and resolved.input_ref.input_id (submission.py:175-183 binds the two equal for an owned input). The script reads that document for each accepted request of a tenant that holds a turned-back input and joins on input_id. The table query for analysis# rows is the product's own (ops/owned_requests.py:290-299). CAVEAT: an accepted request is the acceptance of a request, not proof a report was delivered; the job state (irpt-jobs) and REPORT# rows were not read, so 'with a report' means 'an accepted analysis request names it' (the face's own wording).
reads: table <TABLE>: Scan, FilterExpression begins_with(request_revision,'INPUT#'), projection tenant/request_revision/identity/upload_id/artifact_ref/content_sha256 -- the INPUT# key shape defined at uploads.py:359
table <TABLE>: GetItem tenant+'UPLOAD#'+upload_id, once per input -- the shape at uploads.py:262-264
table <TABLE>: GetItem tenant+'ARTIFACT#'+artifact_id, for the original and the normalized document of each TEMPLATE input and for each composition read -- the shape at reports/repository.py:419
table <TABLE>: Query tenant=:t AND begins_with(request_revision,'analysis#'), once per tenant that holds a turned-back input -- the shape at ops/owned_requests.py:296-298 and acceptance.py:62

bucket <BUCKET>: GetObject with the Key and VersionId the ARTIFACT# row records (reports/repository.py:551-558), for: each template input's retained original, each template input's normalized document, each composition of an accepted request of a tenant with a turned-back input. A blob whose bucket member is not the --bucket argument is counted unreadable (BUCKET_NOT_THE_ARGUMENT), never read.
old_reader: The trunk's infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/intake/template_reader.py at the checkout the script runs in (--old-reader overrides); sha256 at this checkout 76795b75313b076488d6c2f0ed7a8480be92b999efb6886a3ede92b11e916409. Each reader is loaded from a path under its own module name; the trunk module is never imported as the new reader.
method: Per TEMPLATE input: read the original (digest checked against UPLOAD#.content_sha256 and ARTIFACT#.ref.sha256), read the stored template from the normalized document, run the OLD reader (control: equals the stored template, else old_reader_differs), run the NEW reader; if it differs from the stored template, causes = finding codes in the new output not in the stored template (the four named codes, else OTHER:<code>), plus OTHER:NON_FINDING_DIFFERENCE if anything but findings differs; an input is counted once per cause and once in read_differently; turned back = the new output holds an ERROR finding. Any input that cannot be read is counted under unreadable[<code>] and is in none of read_the_same, read_differently, by_cause, turned_back.
output_fields: by_tenant{tenant: the same members except items_scanned and read_at}

self_test.synthetic_content: made-up tickers and numbers; tenants firm-a and firm-b; 11 inputs: clean csv; csv with a Total row (2 accepted requests on 2 days); csv with a repeated header (no request); csv with a two-value account column (1 request); a two-sheet workbook; one csv-lane input; one input with both a Total row and a repeated header; one input whose stored template was altered (old reader differs); one with a missing object; one with a denied read; one with an altered object (digest mismatch); plus 6 accepted requests, one of whose composition object is missing, and requests naming a clean input and a not-turned-back input that must not be counted; the fake table pages its scan at 7 rows and its query at 2.
also_asserted: the output holds no 'portfolio_', 'UP-', 'REQ-', 'ART-', '.csv', '.xlsx', synthetic ticker or account text
only get-item, scan, query and get-object reached the fakes
a denied scan stops the count with code AccessDeniedException (the CLI exits 3 and prints SCAN_FAILED <code>)
self_test.negative_control: the same world read with the new reader replaced by the old one gives read_differently 1 (the altered template only) and turned_back 0: the assertions do not hold on a reader that changes nothing.

invocation_for_the_reader_seat: cd <a checkout at the trunk head that carries the OLD reader>; git show d95cf11106:infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/intake/template_reader.py > <a path outside the checkout>/new_reader.py; python org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_ANLREQ/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_IRPT_ANLREQ~52/r16/count_stored_inputs.py --table <TABLE> --bucket <BUCKET> --region <REGION> --new-reader <that path>/new_reader.py --out <output file>   (the last stdout line is the one JSON object; stderr carries the two reader sha256 values to compare with this record)
what_the_seat_must_hold: dynamodb:Scan, dynamodb:Query, dynamodb:GetItem on the requests table (read-only); s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on the keys of the retained artifacts (the key is written per artifact by the destination policy, reports/composition.py:51-52, and is read from each ARTIFACT# row, not typed); kms:Decrypt on the IRPT key (table and bucket encryption; denied to dell2 per TO-APPLY-Y6 step 0). No write, no list.
not_read: the real table and bucket (no live call was made by this order)
the destination policy that places artifact keys (reporting_destination) and the bucket's real key prefix
job state (irpt-jobs) and REPORT# rows: 'with a report' is an accepted request naming the input, not a delivered report
RETENTION# rows and the retention check (_check_retention) the product applies on every artifact read
NORMALIZATION# rows; CSV-lane originals (counted by lane only); custody and mail inputs (no INPUT# row, not in the scan)
the resident runtime's copy of the reader
the product's authorization on read (the script reads as the seat's identity, not through UploadService)
a request whose composition cannot be read is counted in requests_unreadable, so 'without' may be an undercount by that number
